stem: A boy with a high body mass index is undergoing pubertal review during a broader developmental assessment. What practical point is most important during the examination?

options.text: Watch for a buried penis when assessing pubertal status
Use weight alone instead of examination
Assume pubertal stage from age only
Assess shoe size instead of genital examination

explanation: Watch for a buried penis when assessing pubertal status. In boys with a high BMI, this can make genital examination more difficult, so it is an important practical consideration during pubertal staging.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 94

rationale: A high BMI can obscure genital examination in boys, so clinicians should recognise a buried penis when assessing pubertal status.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a buried penis may be present in boys with high BMI and can affect pubertal assessment.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because pubertal assessment should still be performed as part of the clinical review.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because weight alone does not replace a physical examination of pubertal status.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because age alone is not sufficient to determine pubertal stage.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because shoe size is not part of pubertal assessment.
